b: Please please please don’t stop greeting your neighbours. I love Japan and love living here, but one of the things I hate the most is how cold people can be. I greet everyone in my building, and about half don’t even look at me or respond to me. And I greet them very normally, just a simple こんにちは, not trying to start small talk. Even a simple greeting, studies have shown, can lift people’s mood an

I think it’s a healthy human habit. It’s funny that it’s become unpopular now in Japan because it wasn’t always the case.  I think a lot of people have this way of saying “I’m Japanese and we are shy.” It’s kind of an excuse to not make an effort really.  People in the countryside greet you more often than not. I don’t think it has anything to do with some unspoken rule… It’s just become normalize
